$comment: Aircraft landing gear library.
HOW THIS LIBRARY IS BUILT — read data/SOURCES.md section 5 before using it.
AUTHORITATIVE, taken verbatim from primary sources:
gear designation, wheelbase, main gear OUTER width, MTOW    FAA Aircraft
Characteristics Database
tire size, tire pressure, maximum design taxi weight        manufacturer ACAP
percent of gross weight on the main gear (95 %)             FAA AC 150/5320-6G, G.1.3
DERIVED, exactly, from the above:
tire overall diameter / section width / rim   from the three-part designation
main gear TRACK (centreline to centreline)    from the FAA outer width:
track = outerWidth - (wheelsAcross - 1) * dualSpacing - sectionWidth
The FAA field is explicitly 'distance between outer tires in the main landing
gear' — an OUTSIDE dimension, not the centreline tread. Conflating the two
would put every main wheel in the wrong place, so the track is always derived
rather than assumed to equal it.
CROSS-CHECKED: with the dual spacings recorded here, that derivation
reproduces each manufacturer's separately published tread to within a few
centimetres on all four. test/run.mjs asserts this.
ASSUMED on those four, and declared as such in `assumedFields`:
tandem spacing (2D and 3D gears), and nose gear dual spacing.
Nothing in the sources above constrains them. Set them from FAARFIELD
before using this app's output for pavement work — the app recomputes the
track when you change a dual spacing, so the authoritative outer width is
preserved whatever you enter.
THE WING-PLUS-BODY AIRCRAFT ARE SOURCED THE OTHER WAY ROUND (v1.6).
The 747-400, 747-8 and A380-800 have four main struts, and a single outer
width cannot close that layout — the body gear's offset from the wing gear
is a free parameter no summary table carries. It is why they were absent
for three releases. The manufacturers' own footprint figures (Boeing ACAP
section 7.2, Airbus AC section 7-2-0) publish the track, both gear
positions and every spacing directly, so for these three the geometry is
read off the figure and the OUTER WIDTH BECOMES A CROSS-CHECK instead of
an input. Nothing is assumed on the 747-8 or the A380 at all.
Each is corroborated independently by the FAARFIELD 2.1.1 aircraft library,
whose per-wheel coordinates reproduce every published spacing — including
the A380 body bogie's 20 mm wider middle axle, which `dualSpacingByRow`
exists to carry.
$gearCodes: REMOVED in v1.9. This list was a third hand-maintained copy of the gear
code table — after src/core/schema.js and the app's own dropdown — and it
had already drifted out of the vocabulary FAA Order 5300.7 §6d requires.
Codes now come from src/core/gearcode.js, which derives them from the
naming convention itself, so there is one place for them to be wrong.
